note: The agents that make up a solution's orchestration — the actual steps that fulfil the use case, in the order they run. AUTHORED, not derived. The catalog's own source for most solutions is a single sentence of marketing copy, and splitting that on commas produces 'Enable faster' and 'Lower-risk' as though they were actions. They are outcomes. An architecture that lists outcomes where the work goes tells a reader nothing about what the agent does, so these are written by hand and reviewed. A solution with a real tool schema uses that instead — a declared operation enum beats anything anyone writes here.

fields.name: What the sub-agent is called, as a capability
fields.does: What it actually does, in one line, concrete enough to argue with

contract-review-agent.orchestration: Six agents, run in order, each handing the next a smaller problem

agents.name: Clause extraction
agents.does: Segments the contract and labels every clause by type, so the rest of the run works on clauses rather than pages

agents.name: Standard comparison
agents.does: Diffs each clause against the approved clause library and keeps only what departs from it

agents.name: Risk scoring
agents.does: Rates each departure against the negotiation playbook — acceptable, negotiable, or escalate

agents.name: Precedent lookup
agents.does: Finds how this same clause was settled in prior negotiations, so a position is not re-argued from scratch

agents.name: Redline drafting
agents.does: Writes tracked changes in the document, with a citation on every single change

agents.name: Approval routing
agents.does: Packages the review and sends it to the named approver — and stops there, because sending is a person's decision
